name: Lighting and Material Interaction

# Lighting and Material Interaction


## Overview
This family defines how photometric properties and illumination are computed for splatted primitives, addressing the gap between raw geometric density and visually plausible appearance [G]. It differs from sibling methods by injecting per-primitive shading calculations or baked lighting data into the rendering pipeline, allowing for dynamic lighting interactions, baked global illumination, or direct user editing of material properties per primitive [S1, 3371-per-splat-relighting.md].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Photon Splatting](2832-photon-splatting.md)
[Photon Splatting](#2832-photon-splatting.md) captures direct illumination by rasterizing a light-view map and projecting photons into a sparse voxel octree structure [2832-photon-splatting.md]. It solves the problem of efficiently storing incoming radiance as a direction distribution and energy proportional to the subtended solid angle of the light source [2832-photon-splatting.md]. It differs from [Per-Splat Relighting](3371-per-splat-relighting.md) by [baking lighting](#2169-precomputed-lighting-baking.md) information directly into the voxel data structure during a [pre-computation](#2330-pre-computation.md) phase, rather than computing shading dynamically per splat during rendering [2832-photon-splatting.md, 3371-per-splat-relighting.md]. Choose this method when pre-computing direct illumination into a sparse voxel octree is preferred for static lighting or radiance storage [2832-photon-splatting.md].

### [Per-Splat Relighting](3371-per-splat-relighting.md)
[Per-Splat Relighting](#3371-per-splat-relighting.md) computes a dynamic lighting multiplier for each Gaussian splat based on its world position, normal, ambient occlusion, and confidence, enabling real-time dynamic illumination [3371-per-splat-relighting.md]. It differs from pre-shading by deferring photometric calculations to the rendering pass, allowing interactive light changes while avoiding the complexity of full path tracing by treating each splat as an independent shading unit [3371-per-splat-relighting.md]. Choose this method when dynamic, real-time lighting changes are required without full path tracing overhead [3371-per-splat-relighting.md].

### Splat Painting
**Definition:** Recolorization or shadow additions by checking if a splat center intersects with a spherical brush and adjusting its color value [S1]. **Parameters:** Color channels are stored in 16-bit format to support brushes with smooth falloff and low opacity [S1]. **Pitfalls:** Splat models often do not lend themselves well to painting detailed features (text, lines, symbols) because they represent sparse geometry; models from images use few splats on clean surfaces, preventing detailed color changes [S1]. Color leaks may occur into differently colored parts of a surface if state-of-the-art Gaussian splat reconstructions rarely feature clean and opaque surfaces [S1]. Choose this method when artistic recolorization or shadow additions are needed directly on sparse geometry [S1].

## Background
The techniques described herein originate from the practical requirements of editing and rendering large-scale Gaussian Splat models, specifically detailed in the development of "Splatshop" [S1].

## Sources
[S1] Splatshop: Efficiently Editing Large Gaussian Splat Models, https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.70214, fetched 2026-10-31
